taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 24, Adiantum pedatum aleuticum: fronds close, erect, 25-100 cm. long, arching over to about 70 cm high in the photos.

traits.height_max_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 24, Adiantum pedatum aleuticum: fronds 25-100 cm. long.

traits.life_span.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 24, Adiantum pedatum aleuticum: rhizome thickish, short-creeping or oblique.

traits.woodiness.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 24, Adiantum pedatum aleuticum: a fern.

traits.leaf_habit.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: fronds die back each winter.

traits.reproduction.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 24, Adiantum pedatum aleuticum: sori linear to oblong-lunate, solitary on the truncate lobes.

traits.rosette.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 24, Adiantum pedatum aleuticum: fronds close, from a short rhizome.

traits.perennation.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 24, Adiantum pedatum aleuticum: rhizome thickish, short-creeping or oblique, densely paleaceous.

traits.rhizome_habit.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 24, Adiantum pedatum aleuticum: rhizome short-creeping or oblique.

traits.clonal.note: Hoshizaki and Moran, Fern Grower's Manual (2001) p. 160, Adiantum aleuticum: clump-forming.

traits.leaf_posture.note: Fronds held out flat, the blade level atop its stipe, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 32165872, 33705185, 110933498, 32241494, 140309230, 239146818, 33941328, 145709028): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: blades 10 cm to 30 cm from their foot to the tip of the longest pinna; Abrams (1923 p. 24) gives their breadth, 12-50 cm, and the middle pinnae 12-40 cm long.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 24, Adiantum pedatum aleuticum: stipes stout, much longer than the blades: 15 cm to 60 cm of the 25-100 cm fronds.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 24, Adiantum pedatum aleuticum: blades usually reniform-orbicular, 12-50 cm. broad.

traits.leaf_division.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 24, Adiantum pedatum aleuticum: pinnae 5-14, pinnate.

traits.division_pattern.note: Hoshizaki and Moran, Fern Grower's Manual (2001) p. 148, Adiantum aleuticum: stipe forks into a spreading fan of long narrow pinnae (figure 12.5b); Abrams: pinnae somewhat pedately arranged, arising from the outer side of 2 equal branches surmounting the stipe.

traits.division_order.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 24, Adiantum pedatum aleuticum: pinnae pinnate, the pinnules cleft but not divided.

traits.pinnae.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 24, Adiantum pedatum aleuticum: pinnae 5-14.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 24, Adiantum pedatum aleuticum: blades usually reniform-orbicular.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Hoshizaki and Moran, Fern Grower's Manual (2001) p. 160, Adiantum aleuticum: segment tips sharply denticulate lobes; Abrams (1923 p. 24): pinnules with the lower margin entire, the upper deeply and often unequally cleft.

traits.leaf_colour.note: Hoshizaki and Moran, Fern Grower's Manual (2001) p. 160, Adiantum aleuticum: leaf colour bluish green; sRGB by eye from the photos.

traits.stipe_colour.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 24, Adiantum pedatum aleuticum: stipes castaneous to dark brown; sRGB by eye from the photos.

traits.stipe_scales.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 24, Adiantum pedatum aleuticum: stipes chaffy at the base.

traits.stipe_scale_extent.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 24, Adiantum pedatum aleuticum: stipes chaffy at the base.

traits.sorus_position.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 24, Adiantum pedatum aleuticum: sori solitary on the truncate lobes, at the margin.

traits.indusium.note: Hoshizaki and Moran, Fern Grower's Manual (2001) p. 18, Adiantum: false indusium made from the rolled-under leaf edge.

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: a clump of black-stalked fronds, each a flat, level fan of narrow pinnae of small oblong, bluish-green pinnules.

generator.params.note: Set by hand for western maidenhair fern from its sources and the photos the traits cite; the rest of its growth comes from the library's rules for the form. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 0.26 m tall at 4 years in the open, within its sources' range, as grown. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

sources.title: Project After contributors: hand-set species values
sources.licence: project contribution under the repository's terms

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added with the core-species expansion, phase C batch 3 (2026-10-18): sizes and forms from Abrams, FEIS and Dendrology, counts from photos.
